summary: The root WZN relates to weight. A "wāzin" object is heavy or of full, complete weight, like a "dirham wāzin" which is a full-weight dirham.
lane: وَازِنٌ ذ : see رَاجِحٌ : heavy: (Msb:) or of full weight: (KL:) pl. وُزَّنٌ : see زَالٌّ . You say, دِرْهَمٌ وَازِنٌ (S) A full, or complete, dirhem: (so in a copy of the S:) [ a dirhem of full weight: a heavy dirhem. (PS.)

headwords.def: It (a thing) was heavy: (Msb:) or outweighed, or preponderated; syn. وَجَحَ. (TA.)
هٰ َا يُوَازِنُ هٰ َا This is equiponderant to this. (S.)
He took it, or received it, by weight. (S, * Mgh, Msb, K. *) See an ex. voce سَنْجَةٌ.
A certain star in the left fore leg of Centaurus. (Kzw.) See حَضَارِ.
rel. n. of زِنَةٌ. (S, art. وعد, q. v., voce عِدَةٌ.)

: see رَاجِحٌ: heavy: (Msb:) or of full weight: (KL:) pl. وُزَّنٌ: see زَالٌّ. You say, دِرْهَمٌ وَازِنٌ (S) A full, or complete, dirhem: (so in a copy of the S:) [ a dirhem of full weight: a heavy dirhem. (PS.)
A weighing-instrument; (TA:) a balance; a pair of scales. The weight of a thing. (K, &c.) See مِثْقَالٌ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
